section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section provides the opening header and date of the maamar.
section.t: With the help of Heaven.
Shabbat Parshat Beha'alotecha,
the 9th of Sivan, 5727

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the Alter Rebbe's question about why the haftarah for Shabbat Chanukah begins with "Rani veSimchi" rather than the verse about the golden menorah.
section.t: "Sing and rejoice, O daughter of Zion, etc."
And the Alter Rebbe, in Torah Or,
(Discourses of Chanukah)
the discourse beginning with the word "Zeh",
precisely notes that ostensibly, the haftarah of Shabbat Chanukah should begin with the verse
"And he said to me, etc., I saw and behold a menorah of gold, etc.,"
and why do we begin with "Sing and rejoice, O daughter of Zion"?
And he explains there,
that the connection of "Sing and rejoice, O daughter of Zion" to Chanukah is,
that "daughter of Zion" refers to the Congregation of Israel during the time of exile,
for during the time of the Temple, the Congregation of Israel is called "Zion," and during the time of exile it is called "daughter of Zion,"
as is explained there at length.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section raises the question that the same precise point applies to the haftarah of Shabbat Parshat Beha'alotecha, which also begins with "Rani veSimchi" despite its proximity to the time of the Giving of the Torah.
section.t: And it must be understood,
that the aforementioned precise point
[that the beginning of the haftarah is "Sing and rejoice, O daughter of Zion" and not "I saw and behold a menorah of gold"]
also applies to the haftarah of Shabbat Parshat Beha'alotecha,
which is adjacent to the time of the Giving of our Torah,
for the Giving of the Torah is a matter of freedom,
and nevertheless, the beginning of the haftarah of Shabbat Parshat Beha'alotecha is also "Sing and rejoice, O daughter of Zion."
